turns.content: A LAMP assay for Vibrio cholerae produces an S-shaped fluorescence curve. What does the shape of that trace indicate about the amplification reaction?
A separate colorimetric LAMP tube shows no visible color change, yet its endpoint product gives a ladder-like pattern on agarose gel. What does that gel pattern indicate?
Compare the fluorescence and gel evidence. Does amplification appear to have occurred in each tube, and at what stage of the workflow is the disagreement localized?

Use that localization to identify the most likely reason for the missing color change, distinguishing a failure of amplification from a failure of visual detection. How strongly do the observations support the diagnosis?
What positive-control experiment would most directly test the colorimetric detection chemistry in this assay?
Explain how the proposed control would distinguish an inactive dye or incompatible reaction conditions from failure of the amplification itself.
Calibrate the conclusion given that no dye-function control, buffer-compatibility test, amplicon sequence, or no-template control has been reported.
Do any of the supplied observations directly support a primer-design failure? State what new evidence would be needed to overturn the current localization.
Summarize the best-supported diagnosis, the evidence for amplification, and the most decisive follow-up control.
